- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.44 sentiment → forecast peaks too high).
- Underestimate downward corrections after negative sentiment; model fails to fully adjust when sentiment dips below 0.18.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model reacts to sentiment changes with 2–3 day delay, especially when sentiment is rising.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimate later period (last 10–15 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven forecasts: if sentiment > 0.36, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for market overreaction.
